collection.title: Executive Communication
collection.description: Original practice lines synthesizing Mike Li's publicly described methods for executive presence, managing up, influence, and meeting leadership.
collection.sourceNote: Synthesized from Mike Li's public course syllabus and free lessons. These are original practice lines, not quotations.

methodology: Treat executive communication as structure, delivery, audience judgment, cultural decoding, credibility, and impact rather than accent perfection.
Replace excessive apology with concise ownership, corrective action, and prevention.
Replace excessive praise with authentic, level-ground professional rapport.
Replace excessive context with headline-first senior-level brevity.
Manage up by learning the manager's preferred communication method, anticipating questions and roadblocks, and maintaining a reliable update loop.
Move from reactive task-taker to trusted strategic partner by connecting work to leadership priorities.
Influence without authority through stakeholder mapping, strategic alignment, and deliberate communication before, during, and after decisions.
Prepare crucial meetings around outcomes, resistance, worst-case scenarios, and reframing options.
Own the full meeting cycle: prepare, facilitate, read the room, handle disagreement, recap, assign ownership, and follow through.
Build visibility through useful judgment and proactive communication rather than speaking volume.

sections.title: Headline-first brevity
sections.description: Lead with the conclusion, calibrate detail, and make the decision easy to grasp.
sections.guidance: Lines for concise executive updates, recommendations, escalations, and answers that give the headline before context.

sections.title: Action over apology
sections.description: Own mistakes without shrinking, then move quickly to correction and prevention.
sections.guidance: Lines that acknowledge impact once, state corrective action, explain prevention, and avoid repeated or self-undermining apologies.

sections.title: Level-ground relationships
sections.description: Build authentic rapport without flattery, deference, or performative praise.
sections.guidance: Lines for sincere recognition, respectful challenge, peer-level rapport, and professional confidence with senior leaders.

sections.title: The manager's lens
sections.description: Adapt to how a leader consumes information, makes decisions, and measures success.
sections.guidance: Lines for discovering communication preferences, clarifying expectations, understanding priorities, and tailoring the message.

sections.title: The proactive update loop
sections.description: Create predictable visibility so leaders never need to chase the work.
sections.guidance: Lines that report status, changes, risks, asks, next steps, cadence, and thresholds for escalation.

sections.title: From task to strategy
sections.description: Connect execution to outcomes and become a source of judgment, not just labor.
sections.guidance: Lines that challenge the premise, propose options, connect tasks to goals, anticipate downstream effects, and act as a strategic ally.

sections.title: Stakeholder mapping
sections.description: Identify decision power, incentives, concerns, and the support needed to move.
sections.guidance: Lines for mapping decision makers, influencers, blockers, incentives, hidden dependencies, and coalition gaps.

sections.title: Pre-wire the decision
sections.description: Build understanding and surface objections before the formal meeting.
sections.guidance: Lines for one-on-one pre-wiring, testing a proposal, soliciting objections, incorporating feedback, and preventing meeting surprises.

sections.title: Prepare for high stakes
sections.description: Define the outcome, anticipate resistance, and plan for the worst credible turn.
sections.guidance: Lines for outcome definition, assumptions, likely objections, evidence, concessions, walk-away points, and worst-case responses.

sections.title: Own the room
sections.description: Set the frame, guide participation, read dynamics, and protect the meeting outcome.
sections.guidance: Lines a facilitator uses to open, frame, redirect, invite voices, stop circular debate, manage time, and steer toward a decision.

sections.title: Reframe conflict
sections.description: Turn positional disagreement into a productive discussion of interests and tradeoffs.
sections.guidance: Lines that lower defensiveness, separate intent from impact, name the real tension, preserve face, and propose a shared frame.

sections.title: Close and follow through
sections.description: Convert discussion into a durable decision with owners, dates, and an update path.
sections.guidance: Lines for summarizing decisions, distinguishing open questions, assigning owners, confirming dates, documenting dissent, and following up.

sections.title: Cross-cultural visibility
sections.description: Make judgment visible while communicating confidently across cultural expectations.
sections.guidance: Lines for entering discussion early, asking high-value questions, claiming credit accurately, disagreeing across hierarchy, and clarifying implicit norms.
